description: The organization's audit trail: "what changed on this item?", "what did somebody do last week?", "who moved this and when?". Newest first, one merged feed over item, ticket and order events: assignments, moves, status and category changes, renames, quantity adjustments and stock moves, pack/unpack, code attach/detach, custom-field edits, ticket transitions and checklist results, order transitions. Filters: `itemId` (that one item's history), `actorUserId` (one person; ids from list_members), `sources` (["items"], ["tickets"], ["orders"]), `types` (item event types) and a date window: `since` / `until` as calendar days ("2026-08-01"), `until` included. The server has no timezone and does no conversion; the legacy `dateFrom` / `dateTo` epochs still work, exactly one of each pair. Each row is one flat sentence: `atIso` when, `actorName` who (`viaAgent: true` = done through an AI agent), `type` what happened, `subject` what it happened to, `field` which attribute (the org's own label for a custom field), `from` / `to` the two ends of the change, `amount` where a number moved, and `webUrl`, the record's page in the web app. A row with `featureLocked: true` belongs to a module the organization's plan does not include (maintenance, orders): it is kept because history is a record, and it has no `webUrl`, since there is nothing to open. `limit` is 20 by default, max 50; `nextCursor` pages further back. The filters run after a page is cut, so a filtered page can be EMPTY while `isDone` is false: that page held no match, and older pages may; `isDone: true` means nothing older is left. Requires the manager role.

actorUserId.description: Only this person's actions: the userId from list_members

cursor.description: The `nextCursor` of a previous call; pages further back in time

dateFrom.description: Lower bound as epoch milliseconds (legacy form of `since`; exactly one of the two)

dateTo.description: Upper bound as epoch milliseconds (legacy form of `until`; exactly one of the two)

since.description: Only events from this calendar day onward, "YYYY-MM-DD". The server has no timezone and does no conversion

sources.description: Which records to read events from; absent = all three

types.description: Only these ITEM event types — e.g. ["assigned", "moved", "status_changed", "quantity_adjusted", "custom_field_changed"]. An unknown value returns an error naming the whole valid set. Does not filter ticket or order rows

until.description: Only events up to and INCLUDING this calendar day, "YYYY-MM-DD"

name: list_activity

amount.description: How many moved — stock moves and order lines

atIso.description: When it happened, ISO-8601 UTC timestamp — read THIS one; the server does no timezone conversion

featureLocked.description: Present and true when this event belongs to a module the organization's plan does not include (e.g. maintenance or orders). The row is shown because history is a record, but it carries NO webUrl: there is nothing to open. Absent = a normal row

field.description: Which attribute changed — the organization's own label for a custom field, the checklist line for a ticket check, the item name on an order line

from.description: The value before, already rendered: a name, a status, a number, or a calendar day. Absent when there was none

kind.description: Which record the event belongs to: "item", "ticket" or "order"

note.description: The note the actor left, when any

subject.description: What it happened to: the item or model name, the ticket title, or the order's request text. "—" when the record has since been deleted (the row is kept — an audit trail must not lie by omission)

to.description: The value after, same rendering. Absent when it was cleared

type.description: What happened: assigned | moved | status_changed | renamed | category_changed | quantity_adjusted | stock_moved | contained | removed | code_attached | custom_field_changed | ticket and order transitions | …

viaAgent.description: Present and true when they did it through an AI agent. Absent = they did it themselves in the app

webUrl.description: Link to the record in the web app, for a person to open; the ids are handles for tool calls. Absent on featureLocked rows, which have nowhere to link to

isDone.description: True = this was the last page; there is nothing older to fetch. An EMPTY `events` array while this is false is normal on a filtered read — the filters are applied after the page is cut, so that page simply held no matching rows, and older pages (`nextCursor`) may

nextCursor.description: The `cursor` value for the next page further back in time. Present only while isDone is false

title: List activity
